overview:
Texas's 12th District, anchored in Fort Worth and surrounding Tarrant County areas, leans Republican by about eleven points. Republican incumbent Craig Goldman is running for re-election and has built a substantial financial edge, with roughly $1.5 million on hand. Democrat Angela Rodriguez Prilliman enters as the challenger with no visible fundraising totals or outside support on record.

No public polls or expert race ratings are available for this contest, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, candidate resources, and market pricing. Prediction markets give the Democrat about a six percent chance of winning. The combination of a strongly Republican electorate, an established incumbent, and a large money gap makes Goldman a clear favorite, though the absence of polling leaves some room for uncertainty. A comfortable Republican hold is the expected outcome.
